tldr: Business is back on track in Q2 following Q1 supply constraints.
Q2 FY27 revenue from operations reached Rs. 99.73 crores, up 20.54% YoY and 27.11% QoQ.
Q2 FY27 EBITDA reached Rs. 29.73 crores (up 34.69% YoY) with an EBITDA margin of 29.81%.
Q2 FY27 Profit After Tax (PAT) stood at Rs. 21.33 crores, up 35.79% YoY and 77.57% QoQ.
Gross revenue guidance for the full year was revised to a range of at least Rs. 450 crores to Rs. 500 crores.
management_commentary: Management stated that the business is back on track in Q2 following supply constraints in Q1.
The company has a robust order position, strong balance sheet, and is well-positioned to ride the multi-tiered Indian Railways growth story.
Coil Springs: Steady demand continues across freight stock, coaching stock, and locomotive applications; fitted on Vande Bharat Express. Tenders for 4,000 wagons have been finalized.
Air Springs (LHB coaches): Continuing strong performance, running at around 250 coaches per month.

Forgings: Growth driven entirely by railways to raise capacity utilization. Additional job work for automotive companies has been undertaken to improve utilization and lower operating costs, despite slightly lower margins.
FIBA (Failure Indication and Brake Application system): Received RDSO approval; trial orders expected shortly. Trials will run for 6 to 8 months before commercial production begins.
The company started doing job work for the automotive industry strictly to utilize available capacity in the forging division, reduce production costs, and achieve maximum plant utilization.
The company is in a comfortable position regarding orders, receiving orders daily from zonal railways and wagon builders.

Management stated they are discussing new railway products with rail coach manufacturing facilities (ICF, RCF, MCF) and purchased a new piece of land worth Rs. 10 crores to Rs. 12 crores for company expansion.
Bellows supply delays from ContiTech caused by the war in Q1 have been fully covered up using air freight supplies, resolving the backlog.
Superior EBITDA margins this quarter were driven by operational efficiency and a good set of profitable orders in both coil and air springs.
The forging division is expanding into road construction equipment and working to target the mining sector, and export markets have been initiated for railway components.
Defense product samples have been sent to BEML for the forging division, though approvals are taking time.
The company is debt-free and will fund new projects using its own resources without incurring interest or financial costs.
Management remains committed to delivering an FY27 gross revenue of at least Rs. 450 crores while working towards Rs. 500 crores.
guidance: Gross Revenue Guidance: Revised from Rs. 500 crores down to a range of at least Rs. 450 crores to Rs. 500 crores.
FY28 Growth: Minimum 20% sales growth expected over FY27 executions.
EBITDA Margin Guidance: Expected to be in the range of 27% to 29% for the full year, and expected to remain between 27% and 29% for the next 2 to 3 years.

FIBA Timeline: Regular approval expected by the 1st quarter of next year; trial order of 25 coach sets expected around December 15th for a 6-month trial period; regular supply expected from the 2nd quarter of next year, adding Rs. 10–15 crore sales next year and ~Rs. 30 crore in the subsequent year.
Project Execution: New plant setup to complete by Q1 of the next financial year; revenue contribution expected in FY28–FY29.
segment_performance: Coil Springs: Capacity utilization is almost 80%.
Air Springs: Capacity utilization is around 80%. Air spring margins are higher than coil spring and forging.
Forgings: Plant capacity utilization is at 60%-70% (or around 50% per later comments) driven by automotive job work. Margins are slightly lower than coil and air springs.

FIBA Business: Current market in Indian Railways is Rs. 70 crores to Rs. 80 crores. Expected sales of Rs. 10 crores to Rs. 15 crores for next year, growing to almost Rs. 30 crores in the further year.
Revenue Split: Approximately 40% from air springs, 40% from coil springs, and 20% from forging.

risks: Raw Material and Supply Constraints: Geopolitical situations, wars, and shortages of oil and gas constrained raw material availability in Q1, impacting planned execution.
Margin Pressures: Higher steel, oil, and gas prices could pressure margins in coming quarters.
Liquidated Damages: Strict delivery periods (DP) require careful management to avoid liquidated damages from past delivery delays.
Cash Drag: High cash reserves can lower the Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of the business.
Infrastructure Bottlenecks: Delays in the progress of the dedicated freight corridor limit track availability, impacting rapid scaling of train/coach/wagon deployment.
Approval Delays: Defense sector approvals from BEML and formal approvals for new railway products take time, slowing down initial startup phases.
Demand Shifts: LHB coach demand is expected to decrease after 3 years, though management expects Vande Bharat demand to offset it.
